info.bio:
The Residents son un grupo de música avant-garde ademas de un colectivo performance, han sacado cerca de sesenta albums, creado numerosos filmes cortos, diseñado tres proyectos en CD-ROM, Y seis grandes tours a nivel mundial. A pesar de su larga carrera, de casi cuatro decadas, han mantenido su anonimato. Todas las relaciones públicas, entrevistas y promociones han sido manejadas por sus representantes, The Cryptic Corporation.

Orígenes

Mediante la obscura naturaleza de la banda

scenes.name: The Residents y Ralph Records
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Freaks de Luisiana llegados tarde a la psicodelia que quisieron llevarla más lejos sin saber tocar: anónimos tras sus máscaras de ojo gigante, «representados» por Cryptic Corporation (que en realidad eran ellos mismos) y autosuficientes con Ralph Records, estudio, cuarto oscuro y plató propios. Meet the Residents parodia a los Beatles; The Third Reich 'n' Roll satiriza el pop como totalitarismo; la falsa desaparición antes de Eskimo (1979), recreación sonora del Ártico, es una obra maestra de desinformación; The Commercial Album reduce el pop a cuarenta jingles de un minuto. Pioneros del videoclip.
scenes.family: Art punk y new wave americana

scenes.name: La blank generation (Akron, San Francisco, Manhattan)
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La «blank generation» nace de un vacío moral: la sociedad posindustrial reduce al individuo a un engranaje y la humanidad imagina su mutación en monstruos. La música de la new wave es una de las formas más filosóficas del rock. En Akron (Ohio), Pere Ubu (Modern Dance, «fresco de una civilización al borde del colapso» y folk para la era industrial), Devo, Styrenes, Waitresses, Dead Boys. En San Francisco, el tercer polo: los Residents (Meet The Residents, Not Available, Eskimo), Chrome (space-rock e implosiones industriales), Tuxedomoon, Factrix, Zoogz Rift, Rhythm And Noise, Negativland y Biota. En Manhattan, Suicide (sintetizador y voz; inventan el «psychobilly») y los Feelies.
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

scenes.name: New wave americana
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: La new wave culta, sin prejuicios raciales, abre la puerta al dub y los ritmos negros: Devo y su «devolución» kraftwerkiana; Blondie, que coquetea con la disco y con Moroder; Talking Heads y sus sonidos de raíz; los B-52’s psicotrónicos; y el reverso maldito de San Francisco, Tuxedomoon y The Residents.

podcast.title: Formation and Early Anonymity (1969)
podcast.body: The Residents began as an art collective in Shreveport, Louisiana, in 1969. They were so determined not to have a conventional public image that they did not even have a name for the first two years of their existence. "This is an art collective that began in Shreveport, Louisiana in 1969."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Residents (Shreveport LA, 1969) – No Known Members; Hardy W. Fox Died 2018 Listed as Co-Founder; George Harrison and Claypool Denied
podcast.body: The Residents are an art collective that originated in Shreveport, Louisiana in 1969. By 1971 they were performing in San Francisco. They have never shown their faces or listed any band members — their only point of contact is a company called Cryptic Music. When their debut album Meet the Residents was released in 1974 (parodying the Beatles' Meet the Beatles), some fans believed they were actually the Beatles in disguise. Hardy W. Fox — who claimed to have been a Resident — died in 2018 with his obituary listing him as co-founder and primary songwriter. Other names tied to the band include Homer Cook (unconfirmed), Jay Clem (maybe), and "Charles Boebuck" (apparently a pseudonym for Fox). Contrary to rumors, George Harrison, Les Claypool of Primus, and no member of Devo has ever been in the band. "I can tell you, though, contrary to rumors, George Harrison less clay pool of primus, and no one from Devo has ever been in the residence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Name Evolution (1971-1973)
podcast.body: After their initial period without a name, the collective became "residents uninked" in 1971. By 1973, they were formally known as "The Residents," a name they have continued to use. "In 1971, they became residents uninked. And finally, in 1973, they became known as the residents and continued doing whatever it is that they do even today."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cryptic Corporation Management (1976)
podcast.body: Research into the band's identity often leads back to their management team, The Cryptic Corporation, which was established in 1976. Four men have been connected to this corporation, but all have denied being band members. "This research inevitably leads back to their management team, which is called the cryptic corporation, which was established in 1976. Four men have been connected to the cryptic corporation, but all of them have denied being members of the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Hardy Fox's Revelation and Death (2017-2018)
podcast.body: The only person ever identified as a Resident was Hardy Fox, who made himself known in 2017 as a co-founder and main composer. This revelation came after he had left the band in 2016 following 44 years of involvement. He died of glioblastoma (brain cancer) in 2018, taking all his secrets to the grave. "The only person ever identified as a resident was a guy named Hardy Fox. He made himself known in 2017 as a co-founder and main composer with the group. That revelation came after he left the band in 2016 after 44 years. But then he took all those secrets to the grave with him when he died of brain cancer, glioblastoma in 2018."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Attempts to Identify Members
podcast.body: Many attempts have been made to determine the band's membership, with one researcher even employing spectrographic comparisons of the voices of the band's spokespeople with those on their records, though no concrete identities were confirmed. "There have been many, many attempts to nail down the band's membership with one researcher, even resorting to spectrographic comparisons of the band's spokespeople with the voices on their records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Beatles Speculation (1970s)
podcast.body: In the 1970s, there was widespread speculation that one version of The Residents was actually John, Paul, Ringo, and George in disguise, a rumor that was not true. "At one point in the 1970s, there was speculation that one version of the residence was actually John Paul Ringo and George in disguise. To be try, but not true."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Claypool and Devo Speculation
podcast.body: Les Claypool of Primus was accused of being a member, and members of Devo were also rumored to be involved, but these accusations were not true. "This clay pool of primus has been accused of being a member. Not true, you think? Same thing with members of Devo. Again, not true. Maybe."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Featured on Early New Wave Compilation
podcast.body: The Residents were included in Sire Records' 1977 compilation album, titled "New Wave," which was one of the first of its kind to be labeled as such. The album was described as a "catch-all" where everything was mixed, demonstrating the fluid and often undefined nature of the New Wave movement at the time. "En el refiro están los ramones, están los toquing heads, están de restidense, están todo mezclado, muestra de lo poco claro y lo difuso que era el movimiento new wave o de lo poco definido que estaba."

podcast.title: Influence on Aviador Dro
podcast.body: The Residents were cited as one of the international bands that influenced Aviador Dro, the pioneers of electronic pop in Spain, contributing to their experimental approach. "tomó influencias de bandas como de Residence, Divo o Crafwerk."

srcs.episode: La España Siniestra ｜ La edad de oro del Postpunk y el Dark wave

podcast.title: Prolific Output Despite Anonymity
podcast.body: Despite maintaining complete anonymity, The Residents have released over 60 albums, numerous videos, short films, 10 DVDs, 3 CD-ROMs, and scores for a number of movies, and have embarked on seven world tours. "Yet the residents have released over 60 albums, tons of videos and a bunch of short films along with 10 DVDs, 3 CD-ROMs, and a score of a number of movies. They even embarked on seven world tours, and despite all that, we know nothing about them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Public Appearance Costumes
podcast.body: When The Residents appear in public, they always wear costumes, prominently featuring giant eyeball helmets that cover their heads, and they consistently remain silent. "When they do appear in public, they're in costume with giant eyeball helmets covering their heads. And they never speak."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Worthy "Bent Band" Mention
podcast.body: The Residents were listed as another band considered worthy of inclusion on a list of "bent" or unconventional artists from the alternative era. "The residents."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Robot Helmets and Disguises
xref.body: Daft Punk never appeared in public without covering their heads, typically using elaborate robot-inspired helmets for Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo and Thomas Bangalter. "They're very much like the residents, when we spoke of earlier, because they never appeared in public without covering their heads. In most cases, Guy Manuel de Home in Christo and Thomas Bangaltor have hidden themselves under elaborate helmets inspired by robots."
